{"level": 3, "why": "SCALE ASSUMPTION (stated first so the reader can remap if I have the direction wrong). ASSUMPTION A1: the enumerated levels run 0 = lowest earnings quality / unsupportable, 4 = highest; I am selecting the second-highest band, i.e. "earnings are backed by cash and composition is clean, with identified caveats that stop short of the top band." The bundle does not show me the level wording, so this mapping is mine and is rejectable independently of the evidence below.

WHAT THE BUNDLE ACTUALLY IS. FACT 1 [10-Q Q3 FY2025, acc. 0000723125-25-000021, provenance header]: "Form : 10-Q ... Fiscal period : Q3 FY2025, quarter ended 2025-05-29". FACT 2 [same, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows header]: "Nine Months Ended | May 29, 2025 | May 30, 2024". INFERENCE 3 (from 1, 2): the only cash-flow periods in the bundle are two cumulative nine-month columns; there is no discrete-quarter cash flow statement and no multi-year annual series.

THE ANNOUNCED PRE-COMPUTED INPUTS ARE NOT IN THE BUNDLE.
INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
 needed: a <computed_metrics> block containing the accrual ratio (level and direction), DSO / days inventory / days payable by period, free cash flow after all capex, ROE decomposed into margin × asset turnover × leverage, SBC-to-revenue, and the E-04 / E-07 one-off and adjustment-label tables.
 why: the bundle contains only the 10-Q text — no computed_metrics section, no E-04, no E-07, no peer set. Per the rules I may not derive any of these myself.
 would_change: if an accrual ratio series existed and were rising with a receivables-driven signature, my selection drops at least one level; if a DSO/DIO/DPO series existed and were flat-to-falling alongside the balance-sheet evidence below, the top band would become arguable.
Consequently STEP 1(b) (accrual ratio), STEP 3 as a days-based test, and STEP 4 (ROE decomposition) are unanswered, not answered weakly. What follows uses only statements the filing makes directly.

STEP 1(a) — CASH CONVERSION. FACT 4 [Cash Flows]: "Net income (loss) | $5,338 | $(109)". FACT 5 [Cash Flows]: "Net cash provided by operating activities | 11,795 | 5,102". FACT 6 [Cash Flows]: "Depreciation expense and amortization of intangible assets | 6,203 | 5,794". FACT 7 [Cash Flows]: "Stock-based compensation | 722 | 620". FACT 8 [Cash Flows]: "Receivables | (123) | (2,562)"; "Inventories | 148 | (125)"; "Other current liabilities | (681) | 769". INFERENCE 9 (from 4,5): operating cash flow exceeds net income in both periods present, and in the prior-year period cash flow was positive against a reported net loss. INFERENCE 10 (from 4,5,6,7,8): the excess is dominated by the two large non-cash add-backs (depreciation/amortisation, stock compensation), not by working-capital release — working-capital movements in FY2025 nine months are small in both directions (receivables −123, inventories +148, other current liabilities −681). INFERENCE 11 (from 3,9): "persistent" is the wrong word for a two-period record; the direction of the gap is the same in both periods available, and that is all the bundle supports.

STEP 1(c) — AFTER ALL CAPITAL EXPENDITURE. FACT 12 [Cash Flows]: "Expenditures for property, plant, and equipment | (10,199) | (5,266)". FACT 13 [Cash Flows]: "Proceeds from government incentives | 1,294 | 267". FACT 14 [Leases note]: "Non-cash acquisitions of right-of-use assets Finance leases | 1,247 | 758". FACT 15 [Leases note]: "Cash flows used for financing activities – Finance leases | 218 | 99". FACT 16 [MD&A Liquidity]: "We estimate capital expenditures in 2025 for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $14 billion." INFERENCE 17 (from 5,12): operating cash flow of 11,795 is the larger of the two stated figures against capex of 10,199; the size of the residual is not supplied pre-computed and I am not deriving it. INFERENCE 18 (from 12,14,15): part of the equipment base is being acquired through finance leases that never pass through the investing line — 1,247 of non-cash right-of-use additions in nine months, with only 218 of associated financing cash outflow — so the investing-line capex figure understates the period's economic capital commitment. INFERENCE 19 (from 13,16): government incentive receipts of 1,294 are presented as an investing inflow and management frames full-year capex net of them, so "capex" as reported and "capex funded by the business" are two different numbers in this filing. ASSUMPTION A2 (mine, rejectable): a business whose reported profit is this close to its cash capital outlay has earnings that are real but not yet distributable — this is a judgement about owner-available cash, not a statement the filing makes.

STEP 2(a)(b) — COMPOSITION AND RECURRENCE. FACT 20 [Other Operating (Income) Expense note]: "Patent license charges | $57 | $— | $57 | $—"; "Patent cross-license agreement gain | — | — | — | (200)". FACT 21 [Segment note, Unallocated]: "Lower costs from sale of inventory written down in prior periods | — | — | — | 987". FACT 22 [MD&A Gross Margin]: "Our consolidated gross margin for the first nine months of 2024 reflected $987 million of benefit due to lower costs from the sale of inventories written down to their net realizable value in 2023." FACT 23 [Debt note]: "In the third quarter of 2025, we recognized a $46 million loss in other non-operating income (expense) on prepayment of the 2027 Notes." FACT 24 [Derivatives note]: "We recognized gains of $106 million and $38 million for derivative instruments without hedge accounting designation for the third quarter and first nine months of 2025, respectively." FACT 25 [Derivatives note]: "We recognized losses of $93 million and gains of $52 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2025 ... and offsetting gains of $93 million and losses of $46 million ... for changes in the underlying fair values of the hedged items". FACT 26 [Income Statement]: "Other non-operating income (expense), net | (68) | 10 | (90) | (24)". INFERENCE 27 (from 20,21,22): the two largest non-operating swing items in the comparison — the 200 patent cross-license gain and the 987 inventory-writedown recovery — both sit in the PRIOR-year period and both flattered FY2024, not FY2025; the current period's discrete items (57 patent charge, 46 prepayment loss) run against reported profit. INFERENCE 28 (from 24,25,26): mark-to-market items inside other non-operating are individually material relative to that line (106 derivative gain, 93 hedge loss offset by 93 on the hedged item) but the line itself is −68 for the quarter, so fair-value marks are not a source of the quarter's earnings. INFERENCE 29 (from 20,27): the recurrence test asked for in STEP 2(b) cannot be run properly — E-04's period-appearance table is absent — but within the four columns shown, "patent license charges" appears once and the cross-license gain once, in different years.
FACT 30 [Income Taxes note]: "Effective tax rate | 11.1% | 52.7% | 11.5% | 63.7%". FACT 31 [Income Taxes note]: "The effect of tax incentive arrangements reduced our tax provision by $240 million (benefiting our diluted earnings per share by $0.21) and $623 million (benefiting our diluted earnings per share by $0.55) for the third quarter and first nine months of 2025". FACT 32 [Income Statement]: "Diluted | 1.68 | 0.30 | 4.75 | (0.10)". FACT 33 [MD&A Income Taxes]: "On November 27, 2024, Singapore enacted legislation to implement Pillar Two, which will apply to us starting in 2026. While we are still evaluating the impacts, we expect our effective tax rate for 2026 to be in the high-teens percentage range." INFERENCE 34 (from 30,31,32,33): a stated 0.21 of the quarter's 1.68 diluted EPS comes from conditional Singapore-type tax incentives, and management itself states the effective rate is expected in the high-teens percentage range for 2026 versus 11.1% reported this quarter — so a definable slice of current reported earnings is a tax-regime artefact with a company-stated expiry mechanism, not operating cash generation. FACT 35 [Income Taxes note]: these incentives "are conditional, in part, upon meeting certain business operations and employment thresholds."
FACT 36 [Contingencies]: a jury "found that Micron should pay $425 million for infringement of the ‘912 patent and $20 million for infringement of the ‘417 patent." FACT 37 [Contingencies]: "We are unable to predict the outcome of any of the matters noted above and cannot make a reasonable estimate of the potential loss or range of possible losses." FACT 38 [Contingencies]: "On April 17, 2024, the Patent Trial and Appeal Board ... issued a final written decision ... finding unpatentable the sole asserted claim of the ‘912 patent." INFERENCE 39 (from 36,37,38): reported earnings carry no accrual for an adverse verdict of that size, on the company's stated basis that no reasonable estimate is possible and that the underlying claims have been held unpatentable subject to appeal — a real off-income-statement exposure, but one whose accounting treatment the filing explains rather than obscures.

STEP 2(c) — STOCK COMPENSATION. FACT 40 [SBC note]: "Stock-based compensation expense by caption ... $263 | $217 | $713 | $608". FACT 41 [Income Statement]: "Revenue | $9,301 | $6,811 | $26,063 | $17,361". FACT 42 [SBC note]: "Stock-based compensation expense of $109 million and $99 million was capitalized and remained in inventory as of May 29, 2025 and August 29, 2024". INFERENCE 43 (from 40,41): expensed SBC rose from 608 to 713 across the nine-month comparison while revenue rose from 17,361 to 26,063 — the two moved in the same direction with revenue's rise the larger in absolute dollars. INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE — needed: SBC-as-percent-of-revenue and its trend; why: the ratio is not pre-computed anywhere in the bundle and I may not derive it; would_change: if that ratio were rising, the dilution-funded portion of reported profit grows and my selection weakens; if falling, it strengthens. FACT 44 [Equity note]: "No shares were repurchased in the first nine months of 2025." FACT 45 [Equity statements]: repurchases shown are "Repurchase of stock – withholdings on employee equity awards" of (207), (45) and (39) across the three FY2025 quarters. INFERENCE 46 (from 44,45): SBC dilution is not being offset by buybacks in this period; only tax-withholding share retirements occurred.

STEP 3 — WORKING CAPITAL, FROM BALANCES ONLY. FACT 47 [Receivables note]: "Trade receivables | $5,492 | $5,419"; "Government incentives 1,320 | 834"; total "$7,436 | $6,615". FACT 48 [Inventories note]: "$8,727 | $8,875" with "Finished goods | $1,223 | $1,308". FACT 49 [Income Statement]: "Cost of goods sold | 5,793 | 4,979 | 16,244 | 14,485". FACT 50 [MD&A]: "Total revenue for the third quarter of 2025 increased 37% as compared to the third quarter of 2024". FACT 51 [AP note]: "Accounts payable | $2,757 | $2,726"; "Property, plant, and equipment | 4,370 | 2,925"; total "$8,761 | $7,299". INFERENCE 52 (from 47,50): trade receivables moved from 5,419 to 5,492 between the August 2024 balance date and May 2025 while quarterly revenue rose 37% year over year — the classic receivables-run-ahead pattern is not visible in the balances; the growth in total receivables is in the government-incentives line (834 to 1,320), which is a claim on a government programme, not on a customer. INFERENCE 53 (from 48,49): inventories fell (8,875 to 8,727), including finished goods (1,308 to 1,223), while cost of goods sold rose — inventory is not being built ahead of sales on these balances. INFERENCE 54 (from 51): the increase in the payables total is concentrated in property, plant and equipment payables (2,925 to 4,370), i.e. capital-programme accruals rather than stretched trade payables (accounts payable 2,726 to 2,757). INFERENCE 55 (from 52,53,54): on balances alone, neither of the two classic borrowing-from-next-quarter mechanisms is present. CAVEAT: balances are not days; without the DSO/DIO/DPO series this is a directional read, not the test STEP 3 asked for.
FACT 56 [Revenue note]: "customer prepayments made to secure product supply in future periods and other contract liabilities were $146 million and $907 million, respectively"; "Revenue recognized during the first nine months of 2025 from the beginning balance as of August 29, 2024 included $777 million from shipments against customer prepayments and other contract liabilities." INFERENCE 57 (from 8,56): a stated 777 of nine-month revenue was delivered against cash collected in an earlier period, which is the arithmetic behind the −681 "other current liabilities" drag in operating cash flow — this is revenue recognised without matching current-period cash, and it runs against, not in favour of, the cash-conversion figures in FACT 5. FACT 58 [Revenue note]: "other current liabilities included $807 million and $718 million ... for estimates of consideration payable to customers including estimates for pricing adjustments and returns." INFERENCE 59 (from 58): a customer-consideration estimate of this size is an ongoing management estimate that nets against revenue; the bundle gives two balance points and no roll-forward, so I cannot tell whether the estimate is tightening or loosening.

STEP 4 — RETURN DECOMPOSITION. INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
 needed: ROE decomposed into net margin, asset turnover and leverage, by period.
 why: the bundle contains only raw balances — FACT 60 [Balance Sheets]: "Total equity | 50,748 | 45,131"; "Total assets | $78,397 | $69,416"; "Total liabilities | 27,649 | 24,285" — and FACT 61 [Debt note]: "$538 | $15,003 | $15,541 | $431 | $12,966 | $13,397". No decomposition is supplied and I may not construct one.
 would_change: if the decomposition showed ROE improvement driven by leverage, the quality of the return falls and my selection falls with it; if driven by margin, it holds. FACT 62 [MD&A Consolidated Results]: "Gross margin | 3,508 | 38% | 2,963 | 37% | 1,832 | 27% | 9,819 | 38% | 2,876 | 17%" — margin expansion is directly reported, and FACT 63 [MD&A]: improvements were "primarily due to increases in average selling prices for DRAM products, manufacturing cost reductions, and an increased mix in sales of high-margin cloud products, particularly HBM." INFERENCE 64 (from 61,62,63): both margin and gross debt rose over the period, so the star question in STEP 4 — which of the three moved — is genuinely open on this bundle; I can show margin moved, I cannot show what the return decomposition attributes to it.

WHY THIS BAND AND NOT THE ONE ABOVE. INFERENCE 65 (from 9,10,27,52,53,55): the affirmative evidence is strong — cash flow exceeds profit in both periods shown, the excess is depreciation-driven rather than working-capital-driven, the period's discrete items reduce rather than inflate profit, and the balance sheet shows no receivable or inventory build. INFERENCE 66 (from 3,18,34,43,64): what stops me going higher is not contrary evidence but four specific unresolved items — only two overlapping cumulative periods of cash flow exist, an equipment-financing channel of 1,247 sits outside reported capex, a stated 0.21 of 1.68 quarterly diluted EPS is conditional tax incentive that management expects to compress, and the accrual ratio, days series and ROE decomposition that the task treats as the backbone of the test are simply absent.
CONTEXT THE READER SHOULD WEIGH SEPARATELY. FACT 67 [Risk Factors]: "In the past five years, annual percentage changes in DRAM average selling prices have ranged from plus low-teen percentage range to a minus high-40% range." FACT 68 [Contingencies]: an amended securities class action "alleges defendants made materially false or misleading statements during a putative class period from March 29, 2023 to December 18, 2024, regarding industry supply and demand dynamics and the demand for Micron's products" — an allegation, not a finding. FACT 69 [Item 4]: "the principal executive officer and principal financial officer concluded that those disclosure controls and procedures were effective" and "there were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting." INFERENCE 70 (from 67): earnings quality as measured here is a statement about the relationship between reported profit and cash in these periods, not about the durability of the pricing that produced the profit.", "what_would_move_it_down": "A cash-flow statement covering a later period showing operating cash flow falling below net income with the gap sitting in trade receivables — for example FY2025 full-year trade receivables rising materially faster than the 37% revenue growth against the 5,419 → 5,492 balance shown here — would move me down one level, because it would convert the clean two-period conversion record into a pattern of profit arriving as receivables rather than cash."}
